tier_reason: Peer-reviewed ICS '25 paper (ics25-7.pdf, section 4.2.1) compares CB-SpMV against cusparse_bsrmv from cuSPARSE v12.4, TileSpMV and DASP on 2,843 SuiteSparse matrices, and every number in claimed_speedup appears there. The repo now carries the CB-SpMV code and a cuSPARSE-BSR harness (cb-spmv/run/run_cbspmv.sh, run/run_cusparse.sh, benchmark/cuSparse/) with nvcc flags in the Makefiles, but the host CPU is never stated and the TileSpMV/DASP harnesses are not in the repo, so it stays B rather than A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Paper: CUDA 12.4, driver 550.135. Repo Makefiles: cb-spmv/src/Makefile uses nvcc -O3 -w -arch=sm_89 -Xcompiler -fopenmp; the cuSPARSE baseline (cb-spmv/benchmark/cuSparse/Makefile) uses nvcc -std=c++14 -O3 -arch=sm_89 with -lcusparse (sm_80 for A100). The README's tested environment is RTX 4090, CUDA 12.4, driver 550.144.03.
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed (ICS 2025). The repo now has the CB-SpMV code and a cuSPARSE-BSR benchmark harness with nvcc flags, but the host CPU is not stated and the TileSpMV and DASP comparison harnesses are not in the repo, so the tier is B rather than A. The cuSPARSE baseline is cusparse_bsrmv (the BSR path, best of 2x2/4x4/8x8/16x16 block sizes), not cuSPARSE CSR SpMV. Averages are of per-matrix speedups, and the large maxima (37.54x, 54.27x) are single matrices where BSR pads sparse blocks badly. The advantage over DASP on A100 is only 1.21x, and DASP's own entry in this catalog was retiered to C on harness and correctness evidence. A later commit (2026-09-02, 'bug fix and opt preprocess') postdates the paper, so numbers may differ from the current code. Not a CPU comparison: SuiteSparse, Eigen and PETSc are not compared.

notes: I opened the paper PDF via raw.githubusercontent.com/hpcrl/ICS2025-webpage and checked all the speedups in the text. The metadata matches: Apache-2.0, 29 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-02, active. The repo now ships a benchmark harness (added in the 2026-07-04 commit).

tier_reason: The README confirms a peer-reviewed ICS '26 paper (doi 10.1145/3797905.3807868), but arXiv (CONNECT 403), doi.org and dl.acm.org are egress-blocked, so the speedups come only from WebSearch snippets of the abstract and I opened no numbers page. Following the fbcuda and PFT precedents, I put it at C until someone opens the paper. Opening it could support B.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: CUDA Toolkit 12.4 or later. The Makefile builds with nvcc -std=c++14 -O3 -gencode=arch=compute_61,code=sm_80 (Compute_Capability set by hand) -Xptxas=-v -Xcompiler -Wall --expt-extended-lambda -use_fast_math --expt-relaxed-constexpr; NUM_SM and SHARED_MEMORY_KB are set by hand in include/Common.h. The paper's flags were not checked because the paper is blocked.
corrections.claimed_speedup: From WebSearch snippets of the arXiv 2604.19004 abstract and body (paper not opened): on A100 over 337 square SuiteSparse matrices Ocean achieves 1.4x, 2.6x, 3.5x and 2.0x over spECK, opSparse, TileSpGEMM and HSMU-SpGEMM; overall 1.4x-2.8x on A100 and H100. A snippet also reports, for H100 rectangular matrices, 60.7 GFLOPS for Ocean against 42.6 for spECK and 17.1 for opSparse (about 1.42x and 3.55x, derived from snippet data).
corrections.caveats: No LICENSE file (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt and COPYING all return 404) and no license on the repo page, so usability is reference. Parts of the code are adapted from spECK, plus MurmurHash3 from PeterScott/murmur3 and nlohmann/json, which adds licensing ambiguity. The paper (ICS 2026) is peer-reviewed, but arXiv, doi.org and dl.acm.org were egress-blocked, so the speedups come from WebSearch snippets only, and the cuSPARSE comparison, per-matrix numbers, host CPU and flags could not be checked. The '7.35x/1.43x/1.52x' figures in the lead are OpSparse's own results (arXiv 2206.07244), not Ocean's. The baselines are research codes (spECK, opSparse, TileSpGEMM, HSMU-SpGEMM); whether cuSPARSE SpGEMM was compared is unconfirmed. The README recommends spECK output as ground truth and warns numerical comparison may fail on some matrices due to floating-point error. Tested only on A100 and H100. No CPU baseline (SuiteSparse, Eigen, PETSc).

notes: I found the benchmark_url (arXiv 2604.19004) through WebSearch results but could not open it (CONNECT 403). If the paper becomes reachable, a retier to B is likely. The metadata matches: no license, 7 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-04-21 (README citation), active.
